lag_sensitivity.py.underlying_lag_in_K1694_py: Verified directly: pd.merge_asof(..., direction='backward') on avail_date for spec1-3 (availability may fall inside the outcome month -- honestly labelled ex-post association, not predictive), and direction='backward' on month_start for spec4. Lagged regressors use .shift(1) / .shift(2) each guarded by an explicit month-adjacency mask (adj, adj2), so a gap in the panel cannot silently masquerade as a one- or two-month lag. This is stricter than a bare shift.
lag_sensitivity.py.direction_of_the_test_is_the_honest_one: The docstring reasons correctly that lookahead appears only if the ASSUMED lag is shorter than the ACTUAL one, so it tests longer assumed lags. No grid point reaches |t| >= 1.96; the NULL is invariant across 30-90 days.
